description: Live LLM call against the assembled system_prompt() + user message + tool schemas. Asserts the model picks a specific tool_call OR refuses with a substring. Catches hallucination regressions: e.g. eval#83 msg #549 where Gooni invented 'You're free tomorrow' instead of calling check_calendar_busy.

cases.text: I need to check my schedule for tennis
cases.notes: Original eval saw Gooni hallucinate 'You're free tomorrow' — both hallucinating an answer AND silently inventing tool args (no time anchor) are failures. PASS conditions: (a) call check_calendar_busy with whatever default window the model picks, OR (b) ask a clarifying question about day/time/window before any tool. gpt-4o-mini called the tool; later models (gpt-5.4 + planner-prompt rewrite in PR #89) clarify with 'what window do you want me to check' first. Both safe; only hallucination would fail.

cases.text: what's on my calendar this week

cases.notes: Was previously a refusal case. After #114 (live web_search via Tavily), Rule 5 routes weather queries through the tool. The runner only checks tool selection, not tool output — works even if TAVILY_API_KEY is unset.

cases.text: any news about the elections today
cases.notes: Time-sensitive web-searchable query. Must route to web_search, not invent.

cases.text: what's the current price of Bitcoin?
cases.notes: Prices are web-searchable. Must route to tool, not pull stale training data.

Planner protocol STEP 2: peek before propose/write. Even with explicit time + estimable duration (sport=90m), the first tool call must be check_calendar_busy so any conflict is surfaced in the proposal turn (≤2-turn budget).
High-confidence shortcut (title + start + end all explicit) still peeks busy first. Once the peek confirms no conflict, a follow-up turn calls create_calendar_event — but turn 1 must be the peek.
STEP 1 of planner: if duration can't be estimated from the activity, ASK before any tool. 'project work' has no default — must ask 'how long' (or similar). No tool call expected.
Edit-by-name contract: must resolve event_id via list_upcoming_events before update_calendar_event. LLM cannot synthesize the opaque Google event id.
Delete-by-name contract: must resolve event_id via list_upcoming_events before delete_calendar_event. Plus protocol forces an explicit confirm turn before the actual delete fires.
